reviewed_version: NSF-deposited journal PDF, Annals of Probability 53(1) (2025), 140–174; 35 physical pages
summary: The arbitrary-set inference at the start of Lemma 6.8 fails. Its rectangle-specific use, swapping algebra, and final constants survive the checked reasoning; no failure of Theorem 1.1 is established.

problems.claim: Pairwise l-infinity separation of arbitrary plaquette sets supplies one coordinate globally separating the entire sets.
assumptions: P1 consists of yz-unit plaquettes at x1=-3,+3, x4=0
P2 consists of the corresponding plaquette at x1=0
ambient cubic lattice contains all vertices
problems.check: All cross vertex pairs have l-infinity distance exactly 3; coordinate interval gaps are all zero. There is no global separating coordinate.
problems.result: The proof's first inference fails at the stated generality. The containing-knot conclusion is not refuted by this example.
problems.counterevidence: For axis-aligned rectangles, minimum l-infinity distance equals the maximum of the coordinate interval gaps. The actual application in Proposition 6.1 therefore has a valid separating coordinate.
problems.impact: Supported local proof defect; no demonstrated damage to the central correlation-decay estimate.
problems.correction: Restrict the slicing argument to coordinate-separated plaquette sets or to the application rectangles; handle L<=1 by the trivial covariance bound.
problems.repair_verification: Rectangle distance identity and constant calculation verified analytically; arbitrary-set lemma not repaired.

independent_verification.result: Confirmed under the stated four-dimensional finite lattice assumptions. Plaquettes at first coordinates -3,+3 versus0 give cross distances exactly3; their projection interval gaps are zero in every coordinate, so no one ordered separation of the whole sets exists. For actual rectangles, independent coordinate minimization yields min ||x-y||_infinity=max_i distance(I_1i,I_2i), supplying the single separating coordinate used by the slicing proof. This validates the report's restricted repair, without claiming an arbitrary-set proof.

decisive_checks.result: Measure-preserving bijection cancels the E contribution; two E-complement terms each bounded by sup-norm product times P(Ec).
Union of supports is preserved; same fixed P-decomposition and coordinate map are used twice, and U squared is identity.
A=4*10^24*|G|^2; b>=114+4log|G| gives A exp(-b/2)<=4*10^24 exp(-57)<1, exp(-b/2)<1/2. L>=1 yields desired bound; L<=1 is trivial.

limitations: Full external topological gluing and counting proofs not independently certified
Later Higgs-model appendices not inspected in detail

Bounded correction/supplement search does not establish absence

focused_acceptance_summary.scope: Focused acceptance of the reported Lemma 6.8 proof defect and its actual rectangle-specific application. The admissible plaquette example, source hypotheses, global coordinate-separation requirement and repair boundary were independently checked. Earlier swapping/counting/constant checks remain attributed to the initial review; external topology and later Higgs extensions are not newly certified.
focused_acceptance_summary.assessment_review: Retain Minor. The first inference is false for arbitrary plaquette sets, but the Cartesian-product geometry of the actual rectangles in Theorem 1.1 and Proposition 6.1 provides the needed coordinate separation. The counterexample does not refute the lemma's general conclusion or establish damage to the central correlation theorem.
